title: Codebase guides vs Devin's
summary: We tested the guides our AI writes to explain a codebase against Devin's, on 75 questions checked against the code. Ours answered more correctly (63% vs 52%) and made things up far less often (3% vs 23%).

title: Automations vs Devin
summary: We gave NeoDevEx and Devin the same unattended jobs on a test codebase. We now pass all 10 tests we could run and Devin passes 7, but Devin is still faster and always on.

title: Chat agent vs Devin
summary: Six real coding tasks for both. Ours now gets 98% of facts right (Devin 94%) and costs $0.21 a task against Devin's $0.38. Devin is still faster.

title: AI costs vs Devin
summary: We cut our AI bill per task by about a third with no drop in quality. Investigating the same bug report cost us $0.017 and Devin $0.22.

title: Cost per line of code
summary: Five coding jobs, 15 runs on Gemini 4 Argon, every line counted with git and checked by hidden tests. 100 changed lines cost about 12 cents of AI, and all 15 runs passed. Bigger jobs are cheaper per line.

title: Running our own AI model
summary: We ran free AI models on a computer we rent by the hour instead of paying Google per use. Quality now matches Gemini, but it is slower and only saves money if the computer is kept busy.

title: Setting up at a bank
summary: Our setup assistant learned a simulated bank's tools and rules and connected its private code system in every final run, up from none at first. It no longer claims connections it never made, but results still vary run to run.

title: Moving old apps to new code
summary: Neo ME moved a small Flask blog to Node with 34 of 37 steps the same, for $7.33. A medium Django API did not finish: we stopped it at $59 with 9 of 56 requests the same. The hard app was not run.
